LESSON: SIMPLE POSTURES

Grade: PP2
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: ISLAMIC
Topic 5.1: Simple postures

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Simple postures. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is Eid?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. appreciate and thank Paramatma for His Creation in relation to our existence
2. demonstrate the Omnipresence of Paramatma through prayer, saying and singing bhajans/stavans/shabad/mantras for their spiritual growth
3. demonstrate the understanding that all Scriptures are Holy and that one should handle them carefully and with respect
4. demonstrate their awareness of festivals and participating in them to enhance cohesion and co-existence
5. perform simple rhythmic Yoga exercises to become healthy Citizens g) acquire a sound foundation to develop into an ideal, ethical and moral human being. 208 Strand Sub strand Specific learning outcomes

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SIMPLE POSTURES
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Simple postures helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: SIMPLE POSTURES
Study Simple postures like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Appreciate and thank Paramatma for His Creation in relation to our existence

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate and thank Paramatma for His Creation in relation to our existence. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate and thank Paramatma for His Creation in relation to our existence.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Simple postures” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate and thank Paramatma for His Creation in relation to our existence. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Simple postures is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Simple postures” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: appreciate and thank Paramatma for His Creation in relation to our existence)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Simple postures in your own words. (skill: demonstrate the Omnipresence of Paramatma through prayer, saying and singing bhajans/stavans/shabad/mantras for their spiritual growth)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: demonstrate the understanding that all Scriptures are Holy and that one should handle them carefully and with respect)

Example 4: Show how “Simple postures” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: demonstrate their awareness of festivals and participating in them to enhance cohesion and co-existence)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Simple postures to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: appreciate and thank Paramatma for His Creation in relation to our existence.
3. Practise this skill: demonstrate the Omnipresence of Paramatma through prayer, saying and singing bhajans/stavans/shabad/mantras for their spiritual growth.
4. Practise this skill: demonstrate the understanding that all Scriptures are Holy and that one should handle them carefully and with respect.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Simple postures from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Simple postures: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Simple postures?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is Eid?
2. How do we prepare for (Suggested time – 2 a) describe activities related • Learners discuss in pairs or small Eid?
3. How do we celebrate festival digital devices and other Eid?
4. How many Eids do Islamic festival you celebrate?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Simple postures means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: appreciate and thank Paramatma for His Creation in relation to our existence.
5. Be able to: demonstrate the Omnipresence of Paramatma through prayer, saying and singing bhajans/stavans/shabad/mantras for their spiritual growth.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
